functions.name: com_err
functions.signature: extern void com_err (const char *, long, const char *, ...);
functions.description: Logs or reports an error designated by an error code and a printf-style formatted message. Typical usage is to pass the caller identity (whoami), an error code, and a format string followed by corresponding arguments. If a hook is installed via set_com_err_hook, that hook is invoked to output the message.
requirements: The format string (3rd parameter) must be a valid printf-style format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in the format string.
If a com_err hook is installed, it must accept the same parameters as declared in the hook signature.
Allowance of NULL for the whoami or format string parameters is unknown from this header; callers should not assume NULL is accepted.

functions.name: com_err_va
functions.signature: extern void com_err_va (const char *whoami, errcode_t code, const char *fmt, va_list args);
functions.description: Variant of com_err that accepts a pre-initialized va_list instead of variadic arguments. Intended for wrappers that already have a va_list to format and report an error message identified by an error code.
requirements: args must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to the fmt string.
The format string must be a valid printf-style format string and must match the contents of args.
whoami and fmt NULL-acceptance is unknown from this header; callers should not assume NULL is accepted.

functions.name: error_message
functions.description: Returns a textual description string for the given error code. Typically used to translate an error code into a human-readable message using registered error tables.
requirements: The error code may be any long; mapping to a message depends on initialized/added error tables.
Returned pointer must be treated as read-only; lifetime/ownership unspecified here.

functions.name: set_com_err_hook
functions.signature: extern void (*set_com_err_hook (void (*) (const char *, long, const char *, va_list))) (const char *, long, const char *, va_list);
functions.description: Installs a new com_err hook function that handles error reporting, and returns the previously installed hook. The hook has the signature void hook(const char*, long, const char*, va_list).
requirements: The new hook function pointer must be non-NULL and callable with parameters (whoami, code, fmt, ap).
The hook must interpret fmt/va_list using printf-style semantics.
The returned function pointer (previous hook) should be stored if the caller intends to restore it later.
Thread-safety/async-signal-safety of changing the hook is unknown here; callers should assume no concurrency guarantees unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: reset_com_err_hook
functions.signature: extern void (*reset_com_err_hook (void)) (const char *, long, const char *, va_list);
functions.description: Resets the com_err hook to the library default and returns the previously installed hook function (if any).
requirements: Callers should store the returned previous hook if they intend to reinstall it.
May be called at program initialization or to undo a prior set_com_err_hook; concurrency guarantees are unspecified.

functions.name: init_error_table
functions.signature: extern int init_error_table(const char * const *msgs, long base, int count);
functions.description: Initializes (registers) an error table consisting of count messages starting at the given base error code. Enables error_message to resolve codes in this table.
requirements: msgs must point to an array containing at least count pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
count should be non-negative; specific accepted ranges are not specified here.
base defines the starting error code for msgs[0]; precise mapping beyond this is inferred from common com_err conventions but not specified here.
msgs contents must remain valid for as long as the table is in use unless the implementation copies them (unspecified here).
Return value semantics (0/nonzero) are not documented in this header.

functions.name: set_com_err_gettext
functions.description: Installs a gettext-like translation function used to localize message strings and returns the previously installed translation function. The translator takes a const char* and returns a char*.
requirements: The translator function pointer should be non-NULL and accept a const char* message, returning a pointer to a translated string.
Thread-safety of installing/replacing the translator is unspecified.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned translated strings is unspecified; callers should not free unless documented by the translator.

functions.name: add_error_table
functions.signature: extern errcode_t add_error_table(const struct error_table * et);
functions.description: Adds (registers) an error table described by struct error_table so that error_message can resolve codes from it.
requirements: et must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct error_table with msgs, base, and n_msgs correctly set.
The msgs array must contain at least n_msgs pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
Ownership and required lifetime of et and its msgs are not specified here; callers should ensure they remain valid while in use.

functions.name: remove_error_table
functions.signature: extern errcode_t remove_error_table(const struct error_table * et);
functions.description: Removes (unregisters) a previously added error table so its codes are no longer resolved by error_message.
requirements: et must refer to a table previously added via add_error_table/init routines; passing unknown tables is unspecified.
After removal, callers must not rely on the table being used for lookups.
Any further requirements or error codes returned are not documented here.

functions.name: add_to_error_table
functions.description: Adds a low-level error table list node (implementation detail) to the internal list of error tables. Primarily for internal or compatibility use.
requirements: new_table must be a valid, initialized et_list node; the structure layout is not exposed here.
Callers must ensure new_table remains valid while registered; ownership/lifetime details are unspecified.

functions.name: com_right
functions.signature: extern const char *com_right(struct et_list *list, long code);
functions.description: Looks up and returns a message string for the given error code within the specified error table list. Provided for Heimdall compatibility.
requirements: list must point to a valid et_list representing registered error tables; structure details are opaque here.
code may be any long; successful lookup depends on tables contained in list.
Returned pointer is read-only; lifetime/ownership unspecified.

functions.name: com_right_r
functions.signature: extern const char *com_right_r(struct et_list *list, long code, char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Reentrant/threads-safe variant that writes the message for the given error code into the provided buffer and may also return a pointer to the resulting string. Provided for Heimdall compatibility.
requirements: list must point to a valid et_list.
str must be a valid writable buffer when len > 0; len specifies the buffer size in bytes and should include space for the NUL terminator.
If len is 0, behavior is unspecified by this header; callers should provide a non-zero len.
Message may be truncated to fit len; exact truncation/return semantics are not documented here.
Returned pointer must be treated as read-only; whether it equals str is unspecified.

functions.name: initialize_error_table_r
functions.signature: extern void initialize_error_table_r(struct et_list **list, const char **messages, int num_errors, long base);
functions.description: Initializes an error table list structure with the provided messages array, message count, and base code, returning the resulting list via the out-parameter. Provided for Heimdall compatibility.
requirements: list must be a non-NULL pointer to a location that will receive a pointer to an et_list.
messages must point to an array containing at least num_errors pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
num_errors should be non-negative; specific range limits are not provided here.
base defines the starting code corresponding to messages[0].
The lifetime/ownership of the created et_list and whether messages are copied or referenced is not specified; callers should keep messages valid unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: free_error_table
functions.description: Frees resources associated with an error table list previously initialized/allocated (e.g., by initialize_error_table_r).
requirements: et must be a pointer previously obtained/initialized for use with this API and not already freed.
After calling, et must not be used again.
Exact ownership rules (whether it frees referenced message strings) are not documented here.

functions.name: et_list_lock
functions.description: Acquires an internal lock protecting the error table list. Provided for compatibility with other com_err libraries.
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent et_list_unlock() in the same thread or execution context.
Return value semantics (e.g., 0 for success) are not documented here; callers should check for non-zero/non-success as appropriate based on their environment.
Reentrancy/recursive locking behavior is not specified; avoid recursive locking unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: et_list_unlock
functions.description: Releases the internal lock protecting the error table list. Provided for compatibility with other com_err libraries.
requirements: Should only be called after a successful et_list_lock() by the same thread or execution context.
Return value semantics are not documented here; callers should check for errors as appropriate.
Do not unlock more times than locked.

functions.name: EXT2_INODE
functions.description: Casts a pointer to a large on-disk inode (ext2_inode_large) to the base ext2_inode layout. Use when code needs to access only the common, legacy portion of an inode stored in a large-inode filesystem.
requirements: large_inode must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.

Callers must ensure the inode data has been properly read/initialized from disk before use.

functions.name: ext4_hash_in_dirent
functions.signature: static inline int ext4_hash_in_dirent(const struct ext2_inode *inode)
functions.description: Returns nonzero if directory entries for the given inode are expected to carry a hash (i.e., if the inode has both EXT4_ENCRYPT_FL and EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL flags set). Intended to guide parsing/sizing of dirents in encrypted, casefolded directories.
requirements: inode must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an inode structure whose i_flags field is initialized.
This function does not validate that inode represents a directory; caller should ensure the context is a directory if using the result for dirent layout decisions.

functions.name: ext2fs_dir_rec_len
functions.signature: static inline unsigned int ext2fs_dir_rec_len(__u8 name_len, int extended)
functions.description: Computes the required directory entry record length (rec_len) for a filename of length name_len. The result is 4-byte aligned and includes the directory entry header; if extended is nonzero, space for the ext2_dir_entry_hash structure is also included.
requirements: name_len should be in the valid ext2/3/4 range (0–255).
extended should be 0 or nonzero to indicate whether hashing fields are present; nonzero adds EXT2_DIR_ENTRY_HASH_LEN bytes.
Caller must ensure the returned rec_len fits in the containing directory block and any filesystem-specific dirent constraints.

import random
import struct
import string

# This generator targets free-form NUL-terminated strings consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# across the provided stubs. We craft a corpus of interesting strings that exercise
# different code paths (empty, short, long, printable, mixed, unicode-like, format-like,
# env-var-like), and concatenate several of them separated by newlines so that the fuzzer's
# string provider can slice or consume them as needed. No external I/O.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '

def _rand_ascii(rng, n):
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_word(rng):
    syll = ["com", "err", "ext", "fs", "inode", "block", "group", "dx", "acl", "uuid", "hash"]
    k = rng.randint(1, 3)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(syll) for _ in range(k))

def _fmt_like(rng):
    # Strings resembling printf formats to hit branches, but are just data for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    candidates = [
        "static message",
        "msg=%s",
        "num=%d hex=%x",
        "%s%s%s",
        "two=%d and %d",
        "[%08x] code=%ld name=%s",
        "%% literal percent %% and value=%u",
    ]
    return rng.choice(candidates)

def _env_like(rng):
    keys = ["PATH", "HOME", "USER", "LANG", "LC_ALL", "EXT2FS_TEST", "TMPDIR"]
    vals = ["/usr/bin:/bin", "/home/fuzz", "fuzzer", "C.UTF-8", "en_US.UTF-8", "1", "/tmp"]
    k = rng.choice(keys)
    v = rng.choice(vals)
    return f"{k}={v}"

def _unicodeish(rng, n):
    # UTF-8 like sequences; still valid bytes for free-form text
    # Mix ASCII with multibyte code points
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            out.append(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        elif t < 0.8:
            # 2-byte
            ch = rng.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.extend(chr(ch).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        elif t < 0.95:
            ch = rng.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            out.extend(chr(ch).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        else:
            ch = rng.randint(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out.extend(chr(ch).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    return bytes(out[:n]).decode('utf-8', 'ignore')

def _path_like(rng):
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name = _rand_word(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            name += str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
        parts.append(name)
    prefix = "/" if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
    return prefix + "/".join(parts)

def _bounded_dup(s, cap=256):
    # Emulate code paths where strings are truncated to <=256 including NUL
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    if len(b) + 1 > cap:
        b = b[:cap-1]
    return b + b"\x00"

def _build_corpus(rng):
    corpus = []

    # Empty and very short
    corpus.append(b"\x00")
    corpus.append(b"a\x00")

    # Printable words and combined tokens
    words = [
        "com_err", _rand_word(rng), "ext2", "ext4", "journal", "bitmap", "inode",
        "dx_root", "acl_entry", "group_desc", "super_block"
    ]
    corpus.append(_bounded_dup(" ".join(words[:rng.randint(2, len(words))])))

    # Format-like strings
    for _ in range(3):
        corpus.append(_bounded_dup(_fmt_like(rng)))

    # Environment-like keys
    for _ in range(2):
        corpus.append(_bounded_dup(_env_like(rng)))

    # Paths and filenames (for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME or labels)
    for _ in range(3):
        corpus.append(_bounded_dup(_path_like(rng)))

    # Long ASCII
    corpus.append(_bounded_dup(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(64, 220))))

    # Unicode-like
    corpus.append(_bounded_dup(_unicodeish(rng, rng.randint(40, 180))))

    # Numbers and hex
    nums = [str(rng.randint(0, 2**31-1)) for _ in range(5)]
    hexs = [hex(rng.getrandbits(32)) for _ in range(3)]
    corpus.append(_bounded_dup(" ".join(nums + hexs)))

    # Repeated tokens and separators
    corpus.append(_bounded_dup((";".join(_rand_word(rng) for _ in range(10)))))

    # Specific interesting labels
    specials = [
        "", "ok", "error", "warning", "info", "fatal", "assert", "checksum",
        "crc32c", "uuid", "extent", "directory", "block", "inode%u", "name=%s",
    ]
    for s in specials:
        corpus.append(_bounded_dup(s))

    return corpus

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a randomized selection of entries from the corpus
    corpus = _build_corpus(rng)

    rng.shuffle(corpus)

    # Assemble into a single buffer separated by newlines. Many consumers of FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # pull single strings; providing multiple NUL-terminated segments helps seed different paths.
    # Ensure total size <= MAX_TOTAL.
    out = bytearray()

    # Start with a few targeted entries to match stub expectations early
    primaries = [
        _bounded_dup("static message"),
        _bounded_dup("msg=%s"),
        _bounded_dup("num=%d hex=%x"),
        _bounded_dup("two=%d and %d"),
        _bounded_dup("whoami"),
    ]
    for p in primaries:
        if len(out) + len(p) <= MAX_TOTAL:
            out.extend(p)

    # Add randomized entries until we hit the cap
    for entry in corpus:
        if len(out) + len(entry) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(entry)

    # Ensure buffer not empty and ends with NUL to be safe
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"\x00")
    if out[-1] != 0:
        out.append(0)

    return bytes(out)

    ln = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include a chance of dotfiles and extensions
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(max(1, ln-1)))
        return "." + base
    name = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(ln))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        ext = _rand_choice(r, [".img", ".bin", ".dat", ".raw", ".dev", ".blk"])  # common device-like suffixes
        name += ext
    return name

def _rand_dirs(r: random.Random, depth_min=0, depth_max=4) -> List[str]:
    depth = r.randint(depth_min, depth_max)
    return [_rand_component(r, 1, r.randint(3, 12)) for _ in range(depth)]

def _special_paths(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Paths that commonly exist or are meaningful in Unix-like environments and fuzz sandboxes
    specials = [
        "/dev/null",
        "/dev/zero",
        "/dev/urandom",
        "/dev/random",
        "/dev/full",
        "/dev/loop0",
        "/dev/loop1",
        "/dev/mapper/control",
        "/tmp/ext2.img",
        "/tmp/ext4.img",
        "/tmp/device.img",
        "/tmp/fuzz.img",
        "/tmp/testfile",
        "./ext2.img",
        "./disk.img",
        "./testfile",
        "../relative.img",
        ".",
        "..",
    ]
    # Provide some block-device-like names under /dev to trigger code paths checking device sizes
    for i in range(0, 4):
        specials.append(f"/dev/loop{i}")
    # Add some plausible mount points or directories
    specials.extend([
        "/mnt",
        "/mnt/testfs",
        "/var/tmp/ext.img",
    ])
    # Randomize order deterministically by seed of caller
    r.shuffle(specials)
    return specials

def _build_absolute(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Absolute path: /[dirs]/name
    dirs = _rand_dirs(r)
    leaf = _rand_component(r, 1, 16)
    path = "/" + "/".join(dirs + [leaf]) if dirs else "/" + leaf
    return path

def _build_relative(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = _rand_choice(r, ["./", "../", ""])  # relative forms
    dirs = _rand_dirs(r)
    leaf = _rand_component(r, 1, 16)
    if dirs:
        return prefix + "/".join(dirs + [leaf]) if prefix else "/".join(dirs + [leaf])
    return prefix + leaf

def _maybe_trailing_slash(r: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.15 and len(path) > 1:
        return path.rstrip("/") + "/"
    return path

def _maybe_long(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally produce longer paths (but keep total <= 4096)
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        extra = "/".join(_rand_component(r, 6, 12) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)))
        candidate = base.rstrip("/") + "/" + extra
        if len(candidate) < 4000:
            return candidate
    return base

def _compose_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose among special, absolute, relative
    choices = []
    specials = _special_paths(r)
    choices.extend(specials[:max(3, len(specials)//3)])  # subset of specials
    choices.append(_build_absolute(r))
    choices.append(_build_relative(r))
    path = _rand_choice(r, choices)
    path = _maybe_trailing_slash(r, path)
    path = _maybe_long(r, path)
    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Select a strategy to produce an interesting path
    strategy = r.random()

    if strategy < 0.15:
        # Choose a well-known device file
        path = _rand_choice(r, [
            "/dev/null", "/dev/zero", "/dev/urandom", "/dev/random",
            "/dev/full", "/dev/loop0", "/dev/loop1"
        ])
    elif strategy < 0.30:
        # Common temporary image filenames
        dir_choice = _rand_choice(r, ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", ".", "./", "../"]) \
                     .rstrip("/")
        name = _rand_choice(r, ["ext2.img", "ext3.img", "ext4.img", "disk.img", "fs.img", "device.img"]) \
               if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand_component(r, 4, 10) + _rand_choice(r, [".img", ".bin", ".dat"]) 
        path = dir_choice + "/" + name if dir_choice else name
    elif strategy < 0.70:
        # Generate arbitrary absolute/relative paths
        path = _compose_path(r)
    else:
        # Try directory paths that might be valid for backup or open() calls
        base = _rand_choice(r, ["/tmp", "/mnt", "/var/tmp", ".", "./build", "./out"]).rstrip("/")
        sub = "/".join(_rand_component(r, 3, 10) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)))
        if sub:
            path = f"{base}/{sub}"
        else:
            path = base
        path = _maybe_trailing_slash(r, path)

    # Ensure the output is a sane, non-empty path and within size limits
    if not path:
        path = "/tmp/ext.img"
    if len(path) > 4095:
        path = path[:4095]

    # Return bytes; callers will NUL-terminate if needed
    return path.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a NUL-terminated option string suitable for io_channel_set_options.
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain an option string which is then passed
# to io_channel_set_options(ch, opt.c_str()). Therefore, we generate a configuration option
# string composed of comma-separated key[=value] pairs with reasonable, valid-looking values.
# We vary keys and values to exercise different code paths while keeping inputs plausible.

# Reasonable option keys commonly seen in io layers (platform-agnostic guesses):
# - blksize: block size (integer)
# - ra / readahead: boolean or integer
# - direct / direct_io: boolean
# - sync / dsync / fsync: boolean
# - cache / cache_size: integer
# - write_through / writethrough: boolean
# - discard / trim: boolean
# - zeroout: boolean
# - timeout: integer (ms)
# - retries: integer
# - align: integer (bytes)
# - oflags: bitmask-style string
# - device / path: string (alnum and punctuation)
# - encoding: string token
# - stats: boolean
# - mmap: boolean
# - verify: boolean
# - checksum: enum-like string

BOOL_KEYS = [
    "direct", "direct_io", "sync", "dsync", "fsync", "cache",
    "write_through", "writethrough", "discard", "trim",
    "zeroout", "stats", "mmap", "verify"
]

INT_KEYS = [
    "blksize", "readahead", "ra", "cache_size", "timeout",
    "retries", "align"
]

ENUM_KEYS = {
    "oflags": ["rdonly", "wronly", "rdwr", "append", "create", "truncate", "excl"],
    "encoding": ["utf8", "ascii", "iso8859-1", "none"],
    "checksum": ["off", "crc32c", "xxhash", "sha256"]
}

STRING_KEYS = ["device", "path"]

TRUE_VALUES = ["1", "true", "on", "yes", "enable"]
FALSE_VALUES = ["0", "false", "off", "no", "disable"]

SAFE_BLOCK_SIZES = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]

SAFE_ALIGNS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096]

SAFE_INTS = {
    "readahead": (0, 1 << 20),
    "ra": (0, 1 << 20),
    "cache_size": (0, 1 << 24),
    "timeout": (0, 600000),  # up to 10 minutes
    "retries": (0, 1000),
}

SAFE_PATH_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.:/\\"


def _rand_bool(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(TRUE_VALUES + FALSE_VALUES)


def _rand_int_for_key(rng: random.Random, key: str) -> str:
    if key == "blksize":
        return str(rng.choice(SAFE_BLOCK_SIZES))
    if key == "align":
        return str(rng.choice(SAFE_ALIGNS))
    lo, hi = SAFE_INTS.get(key, (0, 1 << 20))
    return str(rng.randint(lo, hi))


def _rand_enum_for_key(rng: random.Random, key: str) -> str:
    choices = ENUM_KEYS.get(key, ["unknown"])
    # For oflags, sometimes combine with '+' to simulate bitmask-like flags
    if key == "oflags":
        k = rng.randint(1, min(3, len(choices)))
        return "+".join(rng.sample(choices, k))
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _rand_string(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24, charset: str = SAFE_PATH_CHARS) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))


def _make_pair(rng: random.Random, key: str) -> str:
    if key in BOOL_KEYS:
        return f"{key}={_rand_bool(rng)}"
    if key in INT_KEYS:
        return f"{key}={_rand_int_for_key(rng, key)}"
    if key in ENUM_KEYS:
        return f"{key}={_rand_enum_for_key(rng, key)}"
    if key in STRING_KEYS:
        return f"{key}={_rand_string(rng)}"
    # Fallback as boolean flag without value sometimes
    return key if rng.random() < 0.2 else f"{key}={_rand_string(rng, 1, 8, string.ascii_lowercase)}"


def _make_option_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide how many options to include (1..10)
    count = rng.randint(1, 10)
    # Mix keys from all categories
    pool: List[str] = []
    pool.extend(BOOL_KEYS)
    pool.extend(INT_KEYS)
    pool.extend(list(ENUM_KEYS.keys()))
    pool.extend(STRING_KEYS)
    # Add a few generic/unknown keys to exercise unknown-option handling paths
    pool.extend(["throttle", "iobarrier", "exclusive", "nodelay", "prefetch"])  # may be treated as bool or ignored

    # Build unique keys, but allow duplicates occasionally to exercise last-wins logic
    parts: List[str] = []
    used = set()
    for i in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and parts:
            # duplicate a previous key with a new value
            dup_key = parts[rng.randrange(len(parts))].split("=", 1)[0].split(",", 1)[0]
            parts.append(_make_pair(rng, dup_key))
            continue
        key = rng.choice(pool)
        # sometimes emit bare flag without value for boolean-like keys
        if key in BOOL_KEYS and rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append(key)
        else:
            parts.append(_make_pair(rng, key))
        used.add(key)

    # Join with commas; sometimes insert optional whitespace after commas
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        sep = ", "
    else:
        sep = ","
    s = sep.join(parts)

    # Occasionally prefix with a well-known single option to guide parsing
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        prefix = f"blksize={rng.choice(SAFE_BLOCK_SIZES)}"
        s = prefix + (sep if s else "") + s

    # Occasionally add trailing comma or whitespace which many parsers tolerate
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + sep.strip()

    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    opt = _make_option_string(rng)
    # Ensure NUL-terminated since FUZZ_PARAM_STR may provide raw bytes buffer;
    # the fuzzer will likely treat the entire buffer and construct std::string,
    # but we keep compatibility by ending with a NUL for C-string expectations.
    data = opt.encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) >= 4096:
        data = data[:4095]
    # Append a single NUL terminator
    return data + b"\x00"

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzer stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers.
# We craft a corpus of valid, interesting payloads to exercise:
# - io_channel_write_byte: arbitrary byte streams of varying sizes
# - io_channel_write_blk64: block-aligned and patterned buffers
# - ext2fs_crc32_be / ext2fs_crc32c_le: diverse byte patterns and sizes
# - ext2fs_xattr_set: plausible xattr key/value blobs (NUL-terminated keys expected by stub)
# - ext2fs_make_generic_bitmap: small bitmap-like byte arrays
# The generator returns a single bytes buffer; the harness will draw from it for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We pack multiple sub-sections and randomize selection/lengths, while keeping inputs valid.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-:."  # safe printable

# Common file-like payloads
EXT_NAMES = [
    b"user.comment\x00",
    b"user.backup\x00",
    b"user.sha256\x00",
    b"security.selinux\x00",
    b"system.posix_acl_access\x00",
    b"system.posix_acl_default\x00",
    b"trusted.checksum\x00",
    b"encryption.policy\x00",
]

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(n)

def patterned(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of sequential, repeated, and random bytes
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    pat = rng.choice(['seq', 'zero', 'ff', 'alt', 'rand'])
    while remaining > 0:
        l = min(remaining, rng.randint(8, 128))
        if pat == 'seq':
            start = rng.randint(0, 255)
            chunk = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(l))
        elif pat == 'zero':
            chunk = b"\x00" * l
        elif pat == 'ff':
            chunk = b"\xff" * l
        elif pat == 'alt':
            a = rng.randint(0, 255)
            b = rng.randint(0, 255)
            chunk = bytes((a if (i & 1) == 0 else b) for i in range(l))
        else:
            chunk = rng.randbytes(l)
        chunks.append(chunk)
        remaining -= l
        pat = rng.choice(['seq', 'zero', 'ff', 'alt', 'rand'])
    return b"".join(chunks)

def make_block_payload(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a block size commonly used by ext filesystems
    blk_sz = rng.choice([512, 1024, 2048, 4096])
    # keep total <= max_bytes
    max_blocks = max(1, max_bytes // blk_sz)
    count = rng.randint(1, max_blocks)
    total = blk_sz * count
    # build deterministic but varied content per block
    buf = bytearray(total)
    for b in range(count):
        base = b * blk_sz
        # header with magic-ish values
        struct.pack_into('<I', buf, base + 0, 0xEF53EF53)  # ext magic-like pattern
        struct.pack_into('<I', buf, base + 4, rng.getrandbits(32))
        # fill rest with a pattern
        body = patterned(rng, blk_sz - 8)
        buf[base + 8: base + blk_sz] = body
    return bytes(buf)

def make_xattr_kv(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a plausible xattr key (NUL-terminated) + value blob merged
    key = rng.choice(EXT_NAMES)
    # values: small, medium, or structured
    choice = rng.randrange(4)
    if choice == 0:
        val = rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, min(128, max_bytes)))
    elif choice == 1:
        # printable ascii
        ln = rng.randint(0, min(256, max_bytes))
        val = bytes(rng.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(ln))
    elif choice == 2:
        # JSON-like text
        content = {
            0: b'{"enabled":true}',
            1: b'{"level":2}',
            2: b'{"algo":"aes-256-xts"}',
            3: b'{"policy":"v1"}',
        }[rng.randrange(4)]
        val = content
    else:
        # checksum-ish binary
        val = struct.pack('<IQQ', rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(64), rng.getrandbits(64))
    # combine with a small header to keep things varied
    head = struct.pack('<I', len(val))
    blob = head + key + val
    return blob[:max_bytes]

def make_bitmap(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a dense/sparse bitmap up to 256 bytes (as stub caps initial map)
    size = rng.randint(1, min(256, max_bytes))
    density = rng.random()
    bits = bytearray(size)
    if density < 0.33:
        # mostly zeros with occasional ones
        for i in range(size * 8):
            if rng.random() < 0.05:
                bits[i // 8] |= 1 << (i % 8)
    elif density < 0.66:
        # mixed
        for i in range(size * 8):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                bits[i // 8] |= 1 << (i % 8)
    else:
        # mostly ones
        for i in range(size):
            bits[i] = 0xFF
        # clear a few
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, max(1, size // 8))):
            idx = rng.randrange(size)
            bits[idx] = rng.getrandbits(8)
    return bytes(bits)

def make_crc_payload(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Varied lengths including empty
    length_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512]
    ln = rng.choice([x for x in length_choices if x <= max_bytes] or [0])
    # Compose using several sub-patterns
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < ln:
        remain = ln - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
        frag = rng.choice([
            rand_bytes(rng, min(remain, rng.randint(1, 32))),
            patterned(rng, min(remain, rng.randint(1, 64))),
            bytes(rng.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(min(remain, rng.randint(1, 64))))
        ])
        parts.append(frag)
    return b"".join(parts)[:max_bytes]

def assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) Small arbitrary payloads for byte writes and CRCs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        corpus.append(patterned(rng, rng.randint(1, 512)))
    # 2) Block-oriented payloads for write_blk64
    corpus.append(make_block_payload(rng, 2048))
    # 3) Xattr key/value style payloads
    corpus.append(make_xattr_kv(rng, 1024))
    # 4) Bitmap-like payloads
    corpus.append(make_bitmap(rng, 256))
    # 5) CRC specific small/empty inputs
    for _ in range(3):
        corpus.append(make_crc_payload(rng, 512))
    # 6) Some exact sizes like 1, 64, 128, 256, 1024
    for n in [1, 64, 128, 256, 1024]:
        corpus.append(patterned(rng, n))
    # Ensure total number of entries reasonable
    rng.shuffle(corpus)
    return corpus

def mix_corpus(rng: random.Random, corpus: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Choose a strategy: single sample or concatenation of a few
    strategy = rng.random()
    if strategy < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(corpus)
    # Concatenate 2-4 items with small separators to provide more data for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls
    out = bytearray()
    k = rng.randint(2, 4)
    for i in range(k):
        piece = rng.choice(corpus)
        sep = b"" if i == k - 1 else struct.pack('<I', len(piece))
        if len(out) + len(sep) + len(piece) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += sep
        out += piece
    if not out:
        out += rng.choice(corpus)
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = assemble_corpus(rng)
    data = mix_corpus(rng, corpus)
    # Enforce upper bound
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random

from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for ext2/3/4 directory name bytes suitable for hashing APIs.
# The inputs in the fuzzers are FUZZ_PARAM_STR() used as name bytes.
# We aim to produce valid, interesting filename byte sequences (non-NUL),
# covering diverse cases: ASCII, UTF-8 multibyte, casefold edges, dot entries,
# long names near limits, mixed scripts, and odd bytes.

MAX_OUT = 4096
EXT2_NAME_MAX = 255  # Typical max filename length in bytes

ASCII_PRINT = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if c != 47)  # exclude '/'

# Some interesting Unicode sequences (UTF-8 encoded later)
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "é",               # Latin-1 supplement
    "Å",               # Nordic capital
    "ß",               # German sharp s (casefolds to "ss")
    "İ",               # Latin capital I with dot above (Turkish special)
    "ı",               # Latin small dotless i
    "ǆ",               # DZ digraph
    "Ω",               # Greek capital omega
    "ω",               # Greek small omega
    "Ж",               # Cyrillic capital Zhe
    "ж",               # Cyrillic small zhe
    "Καλημέρα",        # Greek word
    "Здравствуйте",   # Russian
    "你好",            # Chinese
    "こんにちは",       # Japanese
    "안녕하세요",         # Korean
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢",        # Fraktur letters (outside BMP)
    "😀",               # Emoji
]

# Bytes that are allowed in Linux filenames except '\x00' and '/'. Include some control-ish and high bytes.
INTERESTING_BYTES = [
    0x01, 0x02, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D,  # controls (note: ext names can contain newlines in practice)
    0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27,
    0x28, 0x29, 0x2a, 0x2b, 0x2c, 0x2d, 0x2e, 0x2f,         # include '.'; exclude '/'
    0x30, 0x39, 0x3d, 0x40, 0x5b, 0x5d, 0x5f, 0x7e,
    0x80, 0x81, 0x8d, 0x8f, 0x90, 0x9d, 0xa0, 0xad, 0xff     # high and odd bytes
]

EDGE_NAMES = [
    b".",
    b"..",
    b".",
    b"...",                    # multiple dots
    b".hidden",               # hidden file
    b".\xff\xfe\xfd",         # dot + high bytes
    b"CON",                   # Windows reserved (not special on ext4)
    b"NUL", b"PRN", b"AUX",
    b"trailing_space ",
    b"trailing_dot.",
    b" leading_space",        # leading space
]

COMMON_PREFIXES = [
    "README", "Makefile", "config", "src", "lib", "include", "usr", "bin",
    "home", "var", "etc", "tmp", "lost+found", "journal",
]

COMMON_SUFFIXES = [
    ".txt", ".c", ".h", ".cpp", ".so", ".ko", ".bin", ".img", ".gz", ".xz",
    ".旧", ".bak", ".old", ".~1~", ".Σ", ".β",
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Avoid '/'; avoid NUL
    s = ''.join(r.choice(ASCII_PRINT) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('ascii')

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a string of about n bytes when encoded; try not to exceed EXT2_NAME_MAX
    s = []
    while True:
        choice = r.randrange(4)
        if choice == 0:
            s.append(r.choice(ASCII_PRINT))
        else:
            s.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
        enc = ''.join(s).encode('utf-8', 'strict')
        if len(enc) >= n:
            break
        if len(enc) > EXT2_NAME_MAX:
            break
    # Trim to at most n bytes without cutting a code point
    enc = ''.join(s).encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    if len(enc) > n:
        # back off by removing last element until <= n
        while s and len(''.join(s).encode('utf-8', 'strict')) > n:
            s.pop()
        enc = ''.join(s).encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    return enc[:EXT2_NAME_MAX]

def _rand_interesting_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        x = r.choice(INTERESTING_BYTES)
        if x == 0x2f:  # '/'
            x = 0x2e   # replace with '.' to keep as a single component
        if x == 0x00:
            x = 0x01
        b.append(x)
    return bytes(b)

def _long_near_limit(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce length near EXT2_NAME_MAX with mixed ASCII/UTF-8
    target = r.randrange(EXT2_NAME_MAX - 8, EXT2_NAME_MAX + 1)
    part1 = _rand_ascii(r, r.randrange(16, 64))
    part2 = _rand_utf8(r, r.randrange(16, 96))
    part3 = _rand_interesting_bytes(r, max(0, target - (len(part1) + len(part2))))
    name = (part1 + part2 + part3)[:EXT2_NAME_MAX]
    if not name:
        name = b"a"
    return name

def _compose_common(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = r.choice(COMMON_PREFIXES)
    mid = ''
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        mid = '-' + ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 8)))
    suf = r.choice(COMMON_SUFFIXES) if r.random() < 0.7 else ''
    s = (base + mid + suf)
    # Occasionally add Unicode at edges
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        s = r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS) + s
    if r.random() < 0.4:

    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:EXT2_NAME_MAX] if b else b"a"

def _edge_name(r: random.Random) -> bytes:

    # Randomly extend with additional characters to test hashing paths beyond dot specials
    if r.random() < 0.5:

    return bytes(name[:EXT2_NAME_MAX])

def _casefold_edges(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Names that differ only by case or by special fold behaviors
    variants = [
        "Istanbul", "istanbul", "İstanbul", "ıstanbul",  # Turkish
        "STRASSE", "straße", "Strasse",                    # sharp s
        "FILE", "file", "FiLe",
        "Σ", "σ", "ς",                                  # Greek sigma
    ]
    s = r.choice(variants)
    # Surround with ASCII to vary
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = r.choice(["-", "_", "."]) + s
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = s + r.choice(["-", "_", "."]) 
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:EXT2_NAME_MAX] if b else b"a"

CHOOSERS = [
    lambda r: _rand_ascii(r, r.randrange(1, 32)),
    lambda r: _rand_utf8(r, r.randrange(8, 64)),
    lambda r: _rand_interesting_bytes(r, r.randrange(1, 48)),
    _long_near_limit,
    _compose_common,
    _edge_name,
    _casefold_edges,
]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose one or combine two strategies to increase diversity while keeping validity
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        data = r.choice(CHOOSERS)(r)
    else:
        a = r.choice(CHOOSERS)(r)
        b = r.choice(CHOOSERS)(r)
        # Join with a non-separator to stay single-component; use '+' or '.'
        join = b"+" if r.random() < 0.5 else b"."
        data = (a + join + b)[:EXT2_NAME_MAX]

    # Ensure no NULs and no slashes; replace if any accidentally present
    data = data.replace(b"\x00", b"\x01").replace(b"/", b".")

    # Guarantee non-empty and within size budget
    if not data:
        data = b"a"
    return data[: min(len(data), MAX_OUT)]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid, interesting extended attribute (xattr) key/value buffers
# for the provided fuzzer stubs which call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for keys and values.
#
# Fuzzer usage summary:
# - ext2fs_xattr_get: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() used for key (NUL is appended by stub)
# - ext2fs_xattr_set: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for key, FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for value
# - ext2fs_xattr_remove: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for key
#
# We therefore generate a buffer that, when split by the fuzzer harness into parameters,
# yields well-formed xattr key strings and plausible value byte strings.
#
# Assumptions about FUZZ_PARAM_STR():
# - It consumes a length-prefixed or delimiter-separated slice from the provided input buffer.
#   Since the exact mechanism isn't specified, we emit a simple structured buffer that many
#   fuzz harnesses support: a sequence of length-prefixed blobs (LE32 length followed by bytes).
# - The returned std::string can contain NULs; the stub then appends an extra NUL for the key.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit between 2 and 4 strings (to satisfy key and optional value needs):
#   [key1, value1, key2, value2...], allowing different stubs to pick what they need.
# - Keys: valid xattr names in namespace.key form, chosen from common namespaces and names,
#         plus edge cases (long names near limits, nested names, case variants, special chars allowed by ext2).
# - Values: arbitrary bytes with varying sizes (including 0-length, small, medium, and near upper bound),
#           but kept under the global 4096 bytes cap.
#
# Xattr key constraints (Linux VFS typical):
# - Format: namespace.name
# - Common namespaces: user, trusted, security, system
# - Allowed chars typically exclude '/' and NUL; we avoid control chars and '/' and ':'.
# - Length limits vary by FS; ext4 allows up to ~255 bytes for name; we keep <= 255.
#
# Output: bytes buffer <= 4096 bytes.

NAMESPACES = [
    "user", "trusted", "security", "system",
]

# Common attribute keys by namespace (non-exhaustive):
COMMON_KEYS = {
    "user": [
        "comment", "description", "mime_type", "tags", "checksum",
        "author", "rating", "backup", "archived", "color",
        "large_name_with_underscores", "CaseSensitiveKey",
    ],
    "trusted": [
        "domain", "integrity", "signature", "seal", "confidential",
    ],
    "security": [
        "selinux", "apparmor", "ima", "evm", "capability",
    ],
    "system": [
        "posix_acl_access", "posix_acl_default", "richacl", "xfsroot",
    ],
}

# Additional edge-case suffixes
EDGE_SUFFIXES = [
    "a", "zz", "key", "k" * 32, "name.with.dots", "name-with-dashes",
    "digits1234567890", "underscore_name", "mixed.Case.Name",
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"


def rand_name(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 255) -> str:
    ns = rng.choice(NAMESPACES)
    # Choose a base key component
    base_list = COMMON_KEYS.get(ns, [])
    if base_list and rng.random() < 0.8:
        comp = rng.choice(base_list)
    else:
        comp = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 16)))
    # Maybe extend with nested components
    parts: List[str] = [comp]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(EDGE_SUFFIXES))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8))))
    name = ns + "." + ".".join(parts)
    # Possibly generate a very long key (but under max)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        pad_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, max_len - len(name)))
        if pad_len > 0:
            name = (name + "." + ("x" * (pad_len - 1)))[:max_len]
    # Ensure it does not exceed max_len
    return name[:max_len]


def rand_value(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Size biased to small and medium, with occasional larger
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.15:
        size = 0
    elif roll < 0.55:
        size = rng.randint(1, 64)
    elif roll < 0.9:
        size = rng.randint(65, 512)
    else:
        size = rng.randint(513, 2048)
    # Generate content with a mix of printable and binary
    out = bytearray()
    modes = ["printable", "binary", "pattern", "unicode"]
    mode = rng.choice(modes)
    if mode == "printable":
        choices = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\n").encode()
        for _ in range(size):
            out.append(choices[rng.randrange(len(choices))])
    elif mode == "binary":
        for _ in range(size):
            out.append(rng.randrange(256))
    elif mode == "pattern":
        # Repeating pattern segments
        segs = [b"\x00\x01\x02\x03", b"ABCD", b"\xff\x00", b"xyz", b"\x7f\x80\x81"]
        while len(out) < size:
            seg = rng.choice(segs)
            out.extend(seg)
        del out[size:]
    else:  # unicode-like UTF-8 bytes
        # Compose from valid UTF-8 code points
        def rand_cp():
            buckets = [
                (0x20, 0x7E), (0x00A0, 0x024F), (0x0400, 0x04FF), (0x1F300, 0x1F64F)
            ]
            lo, hi = rng.choice(buckets)
            return rng.randint(lo, hi)
        s = ''.join(chr(rand_cp()) for _ in range(max(1, size // 2)))
        out = bytearray(s.encode('utf-8'))
        out = out[:size]
        if len(out) < size:
            out.extend(b" ")
            out = out[:size]
    return bytes(out)


def le32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))


def emit_lp_str(blob: bytes) -> bytes:
    return le32(len(blob)) + blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Decide how many strings to emit (keys and values). Ensure at least 2 for set(key,value).
    count = rng.randint(2, 4)

    # Generate alternating key/value pairs, but all entries are generic strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # can consume them in order regardless of which stub runs.
    for i in range(count):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            # key
            key = rand_name(rng)
            parts.append(emit_lp_str(key.encode('utf-8')))
        else:
            # value
            val = rand_value(rng)
            parts.append(emit_lp_str(val))

    buf = b''.join(parts)

    # Enforce global size cap (truncate on boundary, preserving at least two entries)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Try removing the last entries until under cap
        while len(buf) > 4096 and len(parts) > 2:
            parts.pop()
            buf = b''.join(parts)
        if len(buf) > 4096:
            buf = buf[:4096]

    return buf
